primary_source_support.verified_fact: The WAL-reset corruption bug affects WAL-mode releases through 3.51.2 and is fixed in 3.51.3 and later; 3.53.4 is on the fixed side. This does not identify which database/WAL files a productive process is actually using.

grf.hypothesis: Stable PID/process generation plus exact admitted libsqlite3 mapping identity is a sufficient proxy for the productive Frank database/WAL persistence path.
grf.strongest_counter_reality: The same process generation can keep the identical libsqlite3 mapping while closing the intended database and opening a different database/WAL/SHM set.
grf.falsifier: Hold PID, process start identity and attestor-style libsqlite3 mapping identity constant while switching the live SQLite connection from a canonical-looking FRANK_UNIFIED.sqlite fixture to a DECOY.sqlite fixture, then inspect open database/WAL/SHM file descriptors.

unusual_experiment.name: SAME_PROCESS_SQLITE_DATABASE_FD_SPLIT
unusual_experiment.environment: disposable local Linux child process and temporary directory
unusual_experiment.baseline: Child imported Python sqlite3, opened temporary FRANK_UNIFIED.sqlite, enabled WAL, wrote/committed one row, and remained alive for parent /proc observation.
unusual_experiment.intervention: Without changing PID or reloading libsqlite3, child closed the baseline connection and opened temporary DECOY.sqlite in WAL mode, wrote/committed one row, and remained alive for a second /proc observation.

observations.measurement_correction: An initial broad filename filter accidentally treated .sqlite-shm as a SQLite shared-library mapping. Re-analysis of the same captured experiment with the current attestor's libsqlite3.so mapping predicate corrected the mapping comparison to identical; the intervention was not repeated.

limitations: This is a mechanism discriminator, not a productive Frank or Hostinger exploit.
The fixture database was temporary and not canonical Frank state.
The current live attestor is not falsified within its documented narrow scope because it already reports productive_persistence_path_exercised=false.

Observing /proc/<pid>/fd alone is not proposed as sufficient durable persistence authority; productive operation, canonical path/object identity, SQLite build, process generation, state lineage and restart/recovery must be bound together.

collapse.claim: Exact libsqlite3 mapping identity plus stable process generation proves the productive database/WAL target.
Loaded SQLite build identity remains necessary evidence for F-V01-13.
collapse.reason: It answers which SQLite implementation supplies the process, not which state files the productive operation uses.

architecture_delta.new_invariant: A release receipt must not infer productive persistence identity from SQLite library identity. It must causally bind the exact admitted Frank execution generation, accepted SQLite object/build, canonical database/WAL object(s), productive persistence operation and semantic/recovery lineage.
architecture_delta.rollback: No product code changed. Supersede this obligation only if a stronger accepted-host mechanism proves the same causal binding without relying on database-file observation.

next_falsifier.test: On the accepted Hostinger productive Frank service, observe/admit the exact ProductStart and self.root generation, root trust anchor and fixed SQLite 3.53.4 object; exercise a controlled canonical UnifiedDB WAL write/checkpoint; bind the exact opened database/WAL objects to that same generation; then perform clean restart plus downgrade/library-swap/rollback controls and verify fail-closed recovery/state lineage.
